intended_object: An explicit indexing of the 48 norm-2 vectors (roots) of the Golay Construction A lattice by a coordinate i ∈ Fin 24 and a sign, sending (i, false) to 2eᵢ and (i, true) to −2eᵢ. Inferred from the docstring and from how the file uses it.
explanation:
The definition builds an `Equiv` between `Fin 24 × Bool` and the norm-2 vectors of `constructionALattice`, using `Equiv.ofBijective`. The map sends (i, b) to `coordinateRoot i` (which is `Pi.single i 2`) when b is false, and to its negative when b is true. Injectivity is checked coordinate by coordinate. Surjectivity comes from the classification theorem `mem_vectorsOfNorm_two_iff`. So the definition does what its docstring says.

Still, it is not a mathematical notion in its own right. It is a chosen bijection, a piece of bookkeeping that encodes the theorem "the roots are exactly ±2eᵢ" as data. Its only use in the library is to compute `representationNumber 2 = 48` through `Nat.card_congr`, and from that the kissing number. That makes it an auxiliary construction for a counting proof rather than a standard object from the literature. There is nothing to compare against for generality, since it concerns this one specific lattice by design.
